description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'm3b-supplied-match'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: LocaleMatchResult.<init>:103, the unmatched-result invariant, whose range clause is one of the untaken outcomes. A NONE result may not carry a language range; a port that only checked the match type accepts this and then reports a range for a match that does not exist.
The weight clause of the same invariant at :103. Paired with the row above so the two clauses are distinguished rather than one standing in for both.

The match-type clause of :103: a non-NONE type with no locale is refused by the SAME message as the two rows above, which is itself the assertion -- all three malformed unmatched shapes must be rejected under one diagnostic rather than falling through to a different failure.
LocaleMatchResult.<init>:106, the matched-result invariant. Two of its three clauses are never the one that fires; this is the missing-range clause.
The NONE-type clause of :106, which is the shape a port is most likely to accept: every field is populated and only the type contradicts them.

LocaleMatchResult.<init>:111, the effective-weight domain. 1.5 exercises the upper-bound clause; the zero row exercises the lower one. (The non-finite clause is not expressible through this fixture format, since JSON has no NaN or Infinity literal -- a JS caller can produce both, so the port owes those two shapes on its own side.)
The lower-bound clause of :111. A weight of 0 is the value an Accept-Language q=0 would produce, so a port that clamped rather than refused would silently turn an exclusion into a selection.

LocaleMatchResult.<init>:131, whose refusing arm is untaken. The sibling check for the FALLBACK locale at 129 is exercised by the corpus and this one is not, so a fabricated match naming a locale outside its own considered set is accepted today by the corpus's silence.
The control. Every fixture above differs from this one in exactly one field, so each refusal is attributable to that field rather than to the fabricated-match machinery as a whole.
